A flexible face-hugging outer layer pairs with internal ear-EEG, multi-point EMG, a directional microphone array, and an outward-facing speaker — linking capture, recognition, and feedback into one complete loop for low-voice and even silent interaction.

uPoc7616EWXpyfzpoOpE8m.content: Not just another headset — a multimodal interaction system worn at the ear.

45EtPP85Idw0FbVKZWlKpR.content: Where conventional voice devices only listen for sound, Visay Loop reads facial electromyography (EMG), around-ear electroencephalography (EEG), and external speech at the same time. An AI controller handles capture and sensor fusion, then delivers feedback through vibration and an outward-facing speaker. The soft wrapping layer conforms to the masseter, perioral, zygomatic, and submental regions, while the ear-hook frame carries the load — keeping the sensing modules close to their signal sources without sacrificing stability or comfort. It answers a simple question: how can communication stay natural and understandable when speaking out loud is difficult or impossible?

2My0UH6LfkuL4fud7WJC8d.content: The shell and ear-hook frame provide structure while the flexible sensing layer conforms to the face. An internal lightweight high-strength frame handles support and heat dissipation, keeping the device comfortable and stable over long sessions.
